precepts.text: Christ prays that the disciples may be one as we are one: one in spirit and speech, not one entity, or the disciples are one being too.
precepts.point: I and my Father are one is the one scripture the priest quotes; John 17 tells you what one means.
precepts.why:
The priest explaining the sign of the cross as three distinct persons of one essence never opens a Bible. The one scripture he leans on is John 10:30: “I and my Father are one.” That's all he has. But Christ says it again in John 17, and there he tells you what one means.

“And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are.” These are his disciples. If one means one being, one essence, then Christ and the disciples are all one being too. That's not what it's talking about. They are one because they speak the same things, say the same things, in the same spirit.

“Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us”. “And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one”. So are they all one entity? Do they form Voltron, do the fusion dance, become a Megazord? It's madness; it's ridiculous. One means one in spirit and speech, not one entity.

That is why they never bring out the Bible. The trinity was argued out over centuries of councils, borrowed from Greek philosophy, confusion upon confusion, and God is not the author of confusion. The Bible is plain: “to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.” Paul warned, “Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit”.

precepts.text: Those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition.
precepts.point: He opposes and exalts himself above God and sits in the temple of God, with the false image of Christ everyone worships.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Thessalonians calls the man of sin “the son of perdition,” and Christ used that same name in his prayer: “While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name.” This is Christ speaking of the righteous, the elect, in this present world. He kept them in the Father’s name by ministering to them, giving them the word, magnifying the law, breaking down the divisions and showing how they were to be unified under the commandments in the faith of Christ.

“Those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost.” The ones given to him are kept and sealed. John 17 has so many verses that smash the John 3:16 doctrine.

“But the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.” The son of perdition is not kept; he is ordained for destruction. That goes with 2 Esdras 6:9-10: the elect are preserved so that the end, Esau, and then the beginning that follows, Jacob, can come to pass.

Through the process of time Cain elevated himself in his bloodline, putting in place institutions, banking and all the rest, and became a global power. Then comes 2 Thessalonians 2:8: that wicked revealed, “whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth,” by the prophets preaching now, “and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming.”

precepts.text: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.
precepts.point: The truth is the word, and the word says the day cometh that shall burn as an oven.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” Are we free today? Hell no. Do we know the truth today? Not as a nation. So what is the truth that makes free?

Christ prayed, “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.” Sanctify the Israelites through thy truth, mainly the elect, the apostles he was speaking of. And the truth is the word: “thy word is truth.”

So to know the truth is to know what the word says, and the word that is truth says a day is coming that shall burn as an oven. Knowing that truth is what frees our people from the lies, and it is the first step before the Lord saves the poor of his people from the sword of the nations.

precepts.point: Christ is a God, but he is not the true God; he is the true witness of that true God.

precepts.point: The laws of the Most High are everlasting and are the truth, the truth of who we are and what will set us free.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Christ prays the same: “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

The laws of the Most High are everlasting and are the truth, and we are sanctified through it. The word is pure, undefiled, and it is the truth of who we are and what will set us free.

precepts.text: Christians cite this to call Christ the word, but the word that sanctifies is the truth, which is the law.
precepts.point: "To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them." Christians say Jesus is the word and go to John 17:17, "thy word is truth," but the word spoken of is the law; no law means no light, which is why there is no light in christianity.

note.label: Isaiah 8: Maher-shalal-hash-baz, the Snare, and the Law and the Testimony

precepts.why:
“To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.” Christians say Jesus is the word and go to “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

But the word that sanctifies is the truth, and the truth is the law. The word spoken of in Isaiah 8:20 is the law and the testimony. No law means no light, which is why there is no light in christianity: they speak not according to this word. Should not a people seek unto their God, to the law and to the testimony, rather than to familiar spirits and wizards that peep and mutter?

“that they may be one, even as we are one”. Christ gives them the glory the Father gave him. “I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one”. Perfect in one. That's unity.

points: Those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. The son of perdition is Judas the betrayer.

Did Judas blaspheme the Holy Ghost? When Judas realized what he had done, he did not go back and repent and reconcile. Out of guilt he went and hanged himself, and never reconciled. When Peter denied Christ, Peter reconciled. Judas did not.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world: the apostles.

Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word: through the apostles spreading this gospel, which is why we have the word today. He is praying for us as well.

That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us. And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one. Where does that leave any room for that trinity doctrine nonsense? None. It shows that we also are to be one with the Lord, and for us to be one, we must move in the spirit of one: one mind, one body.

That they all may be one, as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us. This is not talking about us joining a Trinity; the Most High and his son are not the same person. Christ says me and the Father are one, and we got to be one with Christ.

That the world may believe that thou hast sent me. Do you realize the world is waiting on the sanctification and unification of the nation of Israel? This whole earth is going to get right once we come together and truly become one.
Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: I have given them thy word, and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world. Having the word means being hated by the world, even by family.
Christ prayed not that the Father take them out of the world but that he keep them from the evil. The path must be walked, and they are sanctified through the truth, thy word is truth.
America is an evil place: it seized another nation's leader in the name of democracy. Those who cannot see it are evil themselves.
The glory which I had with thee before the world was is a power Christ had, lost for a time, and asks back.
